title: Q4 Roadmap Launch Readiness - Postmortem
summary: Postmortem and launch-readiness review for Q4 roadmap rollouts. Discussed incidents during canary, root causes (autoscaler regression + kv cache eviction bug), mitigations (rollback, patch, improved alerts), and next steps for gating launch criteria. Agreed on new runbook items, tighter canary thresholds and stakeholder sign-offs.
transcript:
[00:00] Liam: ok, good morning all, thanks for joining, um this is the Q4 launch postmortem, we'll run through timeline then RCA then actions.
[00:28] Maya: hey, quick note, i'm joining from different time zone so i'll be brief on the canary metrics side.
[00:32] Priya: morning. we pulled logs and traces, got some interesting spikes around 10:12 UTC during the canary.
[00:49] Zoe: there's also the QA report, i uploaded the artifact to the launch board, link in notes, but some of the failure repros were intermittent which made debugging fun, uh not fun.
[01:12] Evan: timeline first, canary started at 10:00, at 10:12 latencies jumped to p95 ~1.2s from baseline 300ms, by 10:20 we saw error rates climb to 4%, and at 10:25 we executed a partial rollback to previous model variant to stop customer impact.
[01:41] Maya: important to call out that the canary load shape was slightly higher than anticipated cause of a synthetic test mis-configuration (we had higher concurrency).
[02:05] Priya: right, and our autoscaler had a regression from the last patch; tl;dr it failed to spin enough dedicated workers because of a threshold check using cpu_util_instant instead of cpu_util_avg, so scaling decisions lagged.
[02:35] Liam: and that combined with the kv cache eviction pattern caused repeated cold starts which amplified latency, yes?
[02:48] Priya: exactly, the KV cache eviction had an off-by-one in the eviction policy so short seqs were evicted more aggressively; cache miss rates spiked which means more model loads.
[03:12] Zoe: QA saw repro when sequences hit 2048 boundary, sometimes the parser mis-labeled tokens leading to cache key mismatch - could be a tokenization edge-case.
[03:36] Evan: ok so two primary factors: autoscaler regression + kv cache eviction bug + test load mismatch. Any other contributing factors?
[03:52] Camila: communication lag ─ on-call wasn't paged quickly because alert thresholds were set to 5% error rate which is too permissive for canary traffic.
[04:08] Liam: good call. so mitigation timeline: we rolled back the autoscaler patch at 10:25, which stabilized scale by 10:34, then a hotfix for the KV eviction was drafted and deployed to canary at 11:15, which fully normalized cache hit rates by 11:40.
[04:36] Maya: metric notes: p50 remained stable, p95 and p99 jumped then recovered; CPU remained okay but GPU memory churn increased during the spike.
[04:58] Priya: traces show repeated model init calls around the spike, that matches the cache evictions.
[05:10] Zoe: there were also a handful of test infra flakiness—some synthetic clients used keep-alive incorrectly, that made the load appear burstier than production patterns.
[05:32] Liam: let's run through the RCA document section by section. who wants to take the autoscaler piece?
[05:45] Priya: i'll take it. so root cause: autoscaler logic used instantaneous CPU util check introduced in PR#7245, which removed smoothing; under sudden bursts, it under-provisioned. regression introduced in 2026-11-29 patch.
[06:12] Maya: reproduce steps are in the ticket, but note that locally the patch looked fine because our load generator didn't mirror the keep-alive behavior.
[06:35] Evan: impact assessment: affected 18% of canary traffic, small but visible; if this had hit prod at scale it'd have been more severe.
[06:52] Camila: mitigation was rollback; long term we need automated canary abort on latency SLO breach not just error rate.
[07:08] Liam: kv cache eviction?
[07:12] Zoe: i can take that. root cause: eviction pointer math used <= instead of < causing an extra slot eviction, repro at boundary sequences, affects key normalization.
[07:29] Priya: confirmed, cache miss rate spike from 2% to 26% at peak.
[07:40] Evan: root cause severity ─ medium. fix is small but we need regression tests for token boundary conditions.
[07:55] Liam: ok, test coverage gaps are noted. now the test infra/misconfig piece?
[08:03] Maya: payload generator used concurrency config X that was copied from an older scenario; synthetic clients used short-lived connections which exaggerated scale. we need a standard canary profile.
[08:20] Camila: Action: enforce canonical canary workload definition in launch checklist.
[08:28] Liam: alerts and runbook?
[08:30] Priya: current alerting thresholds: p95 > 800ms for 5 min, error > 5% for 3 min. For canary we should lower thresholds: p95 > 600ms for 2 min or error > 1% for 1 min to abort canary earlier.
[08:53] Evan: agree. also add a page to runbook to escalate to on-call immediately and page SRE lead.
[09:05] Zoe: QA notes: add a tokenization boundary test matrix and repeat canary with real client keep-alive settings.
[09:18] Liam: let's capture action items and owners.
[09:22] Camila: i'll summarize and send the write-up.
[09:26] [10:00] Liam: ok we'll read through the concrete actions ─ first: revert autoscaler code permanently or add smoothing?
[10:06] Priya: short-term revert + add smoothing test in CI; long-term: smarter autoscaler that accounts for rolling averages and GPU mem pressure signals.
[10:18] Maya: SE to update canary script to use standard connections and concurrency.
[10:24] Zoe: QA to add token boundary unit and e2e tests.
[10:30] Evan: infra to add a canary abort runbook and lower thresholds.
[10:36] Camila: PM to update rollout checklist to require stakeholder sign-offs and smoke test sign-off.
[10:52] Liam: ok let's discuss gating: do we want to re-run canary after fixes or limit to partial rollout? thoughts?
[11:05] Priya: re-run canary end-to-end in staging with real canary profile, then a controlled canary with 1% traffic, auto-abort on p95 breach.
[11:20] Maya: agreed, also run a quick benchmark against dedicated vs hosted to ensure cost/perf assumptions hold. small spreadsheet attached.
[11:34] Zoe: timeline estimate ─ autoscaler revert and CI test in 1-2 days, kv fix + tests 1 day, canary script updates same day, full re-run 2 days after fixes.
[11:50] Liam: so target re-run early next week, fine.
[12:03] Camila: communication plan: notify internal stakeholders, update release calendar, and add a note to customers if we anticipate delayed rollout.
[12:17] Evan: one more item ─ improve observability for KV cache metrics (hit/miss, eviction rate) in dashboard with 1m granularity.
[12:34] Priya: will add panels and alert based on eviction rate > 5% sustained for 3mins.
[12:48] Maya: random transcript noise: we noticed model variant naming got mixed in the rollout script, that's why we rolled back wrong variant first, so fix naming in deploy helper.
[13:08] Zoe: QA also flagged: flaky synthetic clients causing false positives, we should standardize harness.
[13:32] Liam: ok, moving to action items review.
[13:40] Camila: reading them out: 1) Priya - revert autoscaler PR and add smoothing test (due 2026-12-09).
[13:58] Priya: yes.
[14:00] Camila: 2) Zoe - add token boundary unit + e2e (due 2026-12-10).
[14:12] Zoe: noted.
[14:14] Camila: 3) Maya - update canary script and standard workload (due 2026-12-09).
[14:25] Maya: will do.
[14:27] Camila: 4) Evan - add canary abort runbook and lower thresholds (due 2026-12-09).
[14:37] Evan: yep.
[14:39] Camila: 5) Priya - add KV cache dashboards and alert (due 2026-12-09).
[14:49] Priya: copy.
[14:51] Camila: 6) Camila - publish postmortem doc and notify stakeholders (due 2026-12-08 EOD).
[15:02] Liam: any blockers?
[15:06] Priya: only if we need infra access for dashboards, but should be fine.
[15:12] Zoe: tooling time for e2e might need an extra day if we expand matrix.
[15:19] Liam: ok we'll prioritize autoscaler revert and KV fix first.
[15:28] Maya: small note, we should also add canary cost guardrail to prevent synthetic load from ballooning bills.
[15:36] Priya: agreed.
[15:40] Camila: recap and next steps: i'll publish doc and include the action items; we'll schedule a follow-up check-in on 2026-12-10 to validate fixes.
[15:54] Liam: thanks everyone. meeting adjourned.
[16:00] [end of recording]
